name: Mitosis Wave
desc: A live-cell timelapse of a proliferating epithelium: cells tile the field as a jittered sheet of rounded membranes with visible junctions and a stained nucleus each, while a mitotic wave travels across on a moving diagonal front, running the division programme cell by cell -- interphase nucleus condensing to a metaphase plate, anaphase nuclei pulling apart as the cell elongates, a cleavage furrow pinching it into two daughters -- then relaxing back, so divisions ripple endlessly and never converge, with scattered apoptosis darkening the odd cell to keep the sheet churning. Offered as GFP/DAPI fluorescence, H&E histology, phase-contrast, or a flat segmentation label-map.

scale.doc: magnification into the sheet - cells swell, guaranteed visible change

speed.doc: rate the mitotic wave sweeps and cells cycle

density.doc: cell count - how fine the tissue is packed

division.doc: how strongly the wave drives division - elongation, furrow depth, nuclear separation

style.doc: aesthetic: GFP/DAPI fluorescence on black / pink H&E histology / grey phase-contrast with bright halos / flat categorical segmentation mask

seed.doc: deterministic - re-throws the cell packing, phases and division axes
